domain: Islamic Jurisprudence / Legal Philosophy / Commitment Systems
topic_summary: Analysis of the Four Sunni Schools of Jurisprudence (Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali) as a contested kernel case. Each school offers a live reading of the shared jurisprudential-method kernel (Qur'an, Hadith, Ijma, Qiyas) that grounds interpretive authority differently while maintaining mutual recognition. The schools emerged 9th-10th century CE, consolidated by 12th century, and persist across geographic regions without displacement.

key_entities: Hanafi School (founded Abu Hanifa, 8th century; emphasizes qiyas and istihsan; dominant Ottoman Empire, South/Central Asia)
Maliki School (founded Malik ibn Anas, d.795; emphasizes Medinan practice/urf; dominant North/West Africa)
Shafi'i School (founded al-Shafi'i, d.820; standardized hierarchy Qur'an>Hadith>Ijma>Qiyas; dominant East Africa/Southeast Asia)
Hanbali School (founded Ahmad ibn Hanbal, d.855; literalist, minimal qiyas; dominant Arabia; asymmetric recognition)
Hadith (Prophetic tradition, universally accepted but weighted differently)
Ijma (scholarly consensus, defined differently across schools)
Qiyas (analogical reasoning, accepted but applied with varying scope)
key_tensions: Istihsan validity: Hanafi accepts juristic preference as secondary source; Shafi'i rejects entirely
Urf (local custom): Maliki accepts Medinan practice as law source; other three reject
Consensus standards: Hanbali requires unanimous ijma; Hanafi follows Kufa consensus; Maliki follows Medina consensus
Hanbali asymmetric recognition: older three schools recognize Hanbali as legitimate; Hanbali refuses reciprocal recognition, views others as bid'ah

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Shared jurisprudential framework: Qur'an and Hadith as ultimate sources, supplemented by Ijma (consensus) and Qiyas (analogy) where primary sources are silent
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Each school grounds interpretive legitimacy through different methodological hierarchies and source-weighting, but all claim fidelity to the same four-source framework

readings.commitment: Reason and analogy (qiyas) as primary interpretive tools; istihsan (juristic preference) as valid secondary source; flexibility prioritized over strict textualism
readings.authority_grounding: Iraqi scholarly tradition; state patronage (Ottoman Empire); emphasis on rational coherence and practical adaptability
readings.expected_structural_delta: Lower suppression of local variation; higher tolerance for juristic discretion; beneficiary: state administrators needing flexible rulings; victim: textualist purists

readings.commitment: Medinan practice (amal ahl al-Madina) as authoritative embodiment of Sunnah; local custom (urf) as valid law source; living tradition over isolated texts
readings.authority_grounding: Geographic proximity to Prophet's city; continuity of practice as interpretive guide; Malik's judicial authority in Medina
readings.expected_structural_delta: Geographic constraint on authority (Medina privileged); beneficiary: Medinan scholarly lineage; victim: non-Medinan jurists claiming equal interpretive standing

readings.commitment: Strict hierarchy of sources (Qur'an > Hadith > Ijma > Qiyas); standardized methodology; rejection of istihsan and urf; text over practice
readings.authority_grounding: Systematization of legal theory (usul al-fiqh); intellectual synthesis of Medinan and Iraqi traditions; explicit methodological rules
readings.expected_structural_delta: Methodological uniformity constraint; suppression of regional variation; beneficiary: scholars seeking universal framework; victim: practitioners relying on local custom or juristic preference

readings.commitment: Literalist textualism; minimal qiyas; rejection of bid'ah (innovation); Hadith primacy over rational elaboration; unanimous ijma required
readings.authority_grounding: Traditionalist reaction to perceived innovation; direct textual fidelity as sole legitimacy source; refusal to recognize other schools' innovations as valid
readings.expected_structural_delta: Maximum suppression of interpretive flexibility; asymmetric recognition (accepts no other school as fully legitimate); beneficiary: textualist purists; victim: rationalist jurists and practitioners needing adaptive rulings

axiom_contradictions.basis: Hanafi grounds legitimacy in rational coherence and juristic discretion (istihsan); Hanbali grounds legitimacy in strict textual literalism and rejection of rational elaboration as bid'ah. No single framework can hold both 'reason is a valid independent source' and 'reason beyond text is illegitimate innovation' simultaneously.

Maliki grounds authority in living Medinan practice (urf) as embodiment of Sunnah; Shafi'i explicitly rejects urf and local practice as valid sources, requiring direct textual evidence. No framework can hold both 'continuous practice is authoritative' and 'only explicit text is authoritative' as foundational axioms.

Shafi'i accepts analogical reasoning (qiyas) as fourth-tier source after Qur'an/Hadith/Ijma; Hanbali minimizes qiyas to near-rejection, viewing it as rational innovation. While both are textualist, Shafi'i's systematic inclusion of qiyas contradicts Hanbali's axiom that interpretive tools beyond text are suspect.

axes.human_readable: Hanafi Reading: Reason and Juristic Preference
axes.structural_delta: Grounds interpretive authority in rational coherence, qiyas, and istihsan; prioritizes flexibility and practical adaptability over strict textualism
axes.primary_observable: Frequency of istihsan invocation in fatwas; acceptance of juristic discretion in novel cases; geographic spread via Ottoman state patronage
axes.selection_reason: Represents rationalist pole of the kernel contest; highest geographic spread; state-patronage mechanism distinct from other readings

axes.human_readable: Maliki Reading: Medinan Practice as Living Tradition
axes.structural_delta: Grounds interpretive authority in continuous Medinan practice (amal) and local custom (urf) as embodiment of Sunnah; geographic constraint on authority
axes.primary_observable: Invocation of Medinan consensus in legal rulings; acceptance of urf as valid source; North/West African institutional dominance
axes.selection_reason: Unique geographic authority-grounding; practice-over-text axis orthogonal to Hanafi rationalism and Shafi'i systematization

axes.human_readable: Hanbali Reading: Literalist Textualism and Asymmetric Recognition
axes.structural_delta: Grounds interpretive authority in strict textual literalism, minimal qiyas, rejection of bid'ah; refuses to recognize other schools' innovations as legitimate despite receiving recognition from them
axes.primary_observable: Rejection rate of istihsan/urf in fatwas; asymmetric recognition pattern (accepted by others, does not reciprocate); unanimous ijma requirement
axes.selection_reason: Highest epsilon (maximum suppression); asymmetric recognition creates unique structural tension; represents textualist pole opposite Hanafi rationalism

axes.structural_delta: Grounds interpretive authority in explicit hierarchy (Qur'an > Hadith > Ijma > Qiyas) and rejection of istihsan/urf; systematization of usul al-fiqh
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: methodological middle position between Hanafi flexibility and Hanbali literalism; lower structural distinctiveness than selected three; captured as synthesis attempt in omega

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Methodological standardization via explicit source hierarchy and rejection of istihsan/urf
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Middle position between Hanafi rationalism and Hanbali literalism; lower structural distinctiveness; represents synthesis attempt rather than pole of kernel contest; captured in omega as methodological bridge

omegas.description: Shafi'i reading represents attempted methodological synthesis (standardization of usul al-fiqh) rather than a pole of the kernel contest. Does this synthesis function as a Rope (successful coordination) or reveal that the kernel contest is fundamentally between rationalism (Hanafi) and textualism (Hanbali), with Maliki as geographic particularism? Shafi'i's institutional success (East Africa/Southeast Asia) suggests synthesis viability, but its rejection of both istihsan and urf indicates it is not a true middle ground.
omegas.source: Deferred axis shafii_reading + Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium)

omegas.description: By 12th century, classical scholars established consensus that 'the truth does not lie outside of them' — a meta-level agreement that all four readings are legitimate despite contradictory axioms. What is the structural mechanism that permits this licensed plurality? Is it a Scaffold (institutional coordination without resolution) or does it reveal that the kernel itself is ambiguous enough to absorb contradictory readings without fracturing? Hanbali asymmetric recognition (refuses to reciprocate legitimacy) tests this mechanism's limits.
omegas.source: Extraction summary (mutual recognition claim) + Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory)

omegas.description: Geographic distribution correlates with state patronage (Hanafi/Ottoman, Maliki/North Africa, Shafi'i/Southeast Asia, Hanbali/Arabia). Is this a Piton (state power atrophying independent jurisprudential development) or a Mountain (geographic/political constraints that would persist regardless of jurisprudential content)? If Hanafi flexibility attracted Ottoman patronage because it served administrative needs, then state selection is downstream of methodological properties, not upstream.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + extraction entity geographic distribution

omegas.description: Drift status marked 'functioning' because all four schools permit ijtihad (independent reasoning) within their methodological frameworks. But does the licensed plurality structure itself absorb drift by channeling it into school-specific interpretive traditions rather than surfacing as kernel revision? If so, the four-school system may be a Partial drift case (interpretive layer absorbs change without challenging the Qur'an/Hadith/Ijma/Qiyas kernel), not Functioning.
omegas.source: Commitment system recognition (drift_status field) + F03 (Hasty Generalization)

omegas.description: Hanbali reading treats other schools' methodological innovations (istihsan, urf, flexible qiyas) as bid'ah (illegitimate innovation). This creates asymmetric recognition: Hanbali is accepted by others but refuses reciprocal legitimacy. Is this a Snare (Hanbali textualism suppresses adaptive jurisprudence) or does it reveal that the kernel contest is actually about the bid'ah boundary itself — what counts as fidelity vs. innovation? If the latter, then the kernel is not 'Qur'an/Hadith/Ijma/Qiyas' but 'the permissible scope of interpretive elaboration.'
omegas.source: Hanbali asymmetric recognition tension + Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory)
